scoring_justification: Properties can be recomputed from stress-strain data; structural trends are derived from recomputed values. T1 is feasible.

hidden_assets.purpose: trend thresholds for thickness/temperature dependence and curve shape
hidden_assets.source_provenance: derived from paper's explicit narrative: decreasing E and UTS with thickness, plateau beyond 4nm, 1nm has >50% higher values, and temperature-induced degradation with sharp drop above 700K; shape description: 1nm curve has two crests with peak after first, thicker films peak at first crest.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: based on paper's own description of trends, not fabricated.

outputs.description: Stress-strain data points for all simulated conditions; the checker recomputes Young's modulus and ultimate tensile strength from these and verifies thickness/temperature/shape trends.
Agent-extracted mechanical properties; the checker compares against its own recomputed values for consistency.

output_contract.notes: Only graphene-covered nanofilm simulations under uniaxial tension are reproduced; pristine silicon films and VMD visualization are excluded per task scope. The required simulation conditions are: thicknesses 1,2,3,4,5,6 nm at 300 K, and 1 nm at temperatures 200,300,500,700,900 K.

steps.description: Validate required columns and presence of required simulation conditions
Check monotonic decrease of E and UTS with thickness and plateau for thickness>=4nm
Check monotonic decrease of properties with temperature and sufficient drop above 700K
Check stress-strain curve shape for 1nm vs thicker films
Check self-consistency: agent-reported properties match recomputed from raw data within 1%
